pushback_verification: All 12 verified against current artifact content before disposition; none suppressed as stale. Two verifications widened their finding: the CRITICAL's single cited site was one of six carrying the retired propose-side field names, and the citation-divergence finding's task also still held the pre-walk unconstrained discovery fallback the external round had already replaced in the spec. Both were swept as part of the same resolution rather than left for a later pass.

resolutions.title: Zero-engine-git requirement still names pr_url/pr_state on the propose emit — retired by the pr_attachment record
resolutions.action: Rewrote the engine-surface clause to name the structured `pr_attachment` object on propose/ff and the flat `pr_url`/`pr_state` pair on archive only, with the asymmetry justified (propose/ff RESOLVE an attachment; archive reports observed state) and the fail-loud consequence stated: `pr_url` on a propose payload is a REJECTED key, not a tolerated alias. The sweep found FIVE more residue sites the finding did not name — proposal.md's zero-engine-git bullet, its run-summary-emit capability line, its emit-composition capability line, design.md's Touchpoints row, and a propose scenario still eliding the retired fields — all corrected; every surviving `pr_url` reference is now archive-scoped.

resolutions.title: Archive tail never states it must be ON the attachment's branch — a HEAD mismatch pushes the archive commit elsewhere
resolutions.action: Ratified option A (skip-only). Added a HEAD PRECONDITION to the tail: compare HEAD's branch to `pr_attachment.branch` before staging; on mismatch or a locally-absent branch, SKIP with a one-line note naming both branches and the literal `git switch <branch>` recovery. Never checkout, never stash — a working-tree mutation here would fire after the user consented to a sync-and-move. The requirement names the failure it prevents: without the check the archive writes commit and push to `main`, every step reports success, the ordering invariant reads as satisfied, and a PR is flipped READY announcing work it does not contain. Task 4.1b + a harness case asserting zero commits on the default branch.
resolutions.resolution: A — skip-only; verify HEAD, never checkout, and make the note carry the exact recovery command

resolutions.title: "Open the program PR if it does not yet exist" specifies no existence check — Shape A's one-PR rule is unenforced at propose
resolutions.action: Required the SAME four-axis constrained query the archive tail uses before opening a program PR: exactly one survivor = ADOPT it into this propose's `pr_attachment` and create nothing; zero = create; several = ambiguity skip; query ERROR = degradation skip, never create-on-error, since a duplicate program PR is the one outcome Shape A cannot represent. New scenario + task 3.1 + harness case 6.2d asserting no `gh pr create` fires against the stub's log when a program PR already exists.

resolutions.title: Tail scope is attachment-driven and config-driven at once; an attached change under a later `pr: never` is undefined
resolutions.action: Ratified option A (attachment authority). The SCOPE sentence now reads: the tail runs whenever a `pr_attachment` resolves, whatever `pr:` reads at archive time; UNATTACHED changes end exactly as pre-capability. Justified as the SAME freeze-at-commitment rule the citation carries one requirement earlier — config selects the regime at the attaching invocation and every later seam follows the frozen record. Setting `pr: never` stops new attachments without abandoning an open PR, because a draft PR that never closes is invisible while writes under a changed key are legible in the PR itself; a user who means to abandon one closes it and discovery then finds nothing.
resolutions.resolution: A — attachment wins; config is read only at the attaching invocation

options_presented.label: A
options_presented.body: Attachment wins: the tail runs whenever a pr_attachment resolves, regardless of the current pr: value.

options_presented.label: B
options_presented.body: Config wins: pr: never at archive suppresses the tail even for an attached change, with a note naming the PR left DRAFT.

resolutions.title: Arc-done readout's stop condition ("until the PR is no longer draft") names no source for the PR's current state
resolutions.action: The readout now reads the CURRENT state live via a READ-ONLY `gh pr view --json isDraft` against the located URL, never the frozen `pr_attachment.state` (permanently `"draft"` by construction, so a readout gated on it would nag forever after the human flips READY). The read is permitted because it is an observation, not an outward write — the zero-engine-git rule constrains the ENGINE, not a body's reads. A failed or unavailable query still SURFACES the readout with a `state unverified` note: an unverifiable state must never suppress the one surfacing the program relies on.

resolutions.title: Archive tail consumes "the RESOLVED REMOTE" and "the RESOLVED BASE" with no resolution rule in its own scope
resolutions.action: Ratified option A (hoist). Added a SHARED requirement `Remote and default-branch resolution` to `orbit-pr-lifecycle`, consumed by BOTH seams; propose's block shrank to a citation keeping only its own preconditions (name collision, dirty tree, branch compatibility), and the tail's four-axis query now cites the shared algorithm with an explicit rule that an unresolvable remote or base is a DEGRADATION SKIP, never a zero result. Chosen over the cheaper one-sentence cite because the reviewer's cross-cutting thesis was seam asymmetry: leaving the algorithm inside a requirement titled 'at propose' would have the next seam borrow it again. Task 3.1a implements it once as a reusable body step with a grep-test that no seam resolves independently.
resolutions.resolution: A — hoist into a shared orbit-pr-lifecycle requirement; both seams cite it

options_presented.label: A
options_presented.body: Hoist the resolution algorithm into a shared requirement in orbit-pr-lifecycle; both seams cite it.

options_presented.label: B
options_presented.body: Leave it in propose and add one citing sentence to the archive tail.

resolutions.title: Propose's commit scope is unenumerated and its dirty-tree guard covers only TRACKED modifications
resolutions.action: Gave propose the archive tail's discipline and said why it is the same reason — this commit becomes the first commit of a PR: an ENUMERATED file list (generated artifacts, moved staging material, and the `orbit/explore/<name>/` deletions), with `git add -A` and bare directory-prefix staging PROHIBITED. Named the trap explicitly: the artifacts are newly created and therefore untracked, so `-A` is the obvious reach and exactly what sweeps an unrelated untracked file into a PR about to be published. Unrelated untracked paths do not trigger the dirty skip but ARE named in the note. New scenario + task 3.1b + harness case.

resolutions.title: The citation-edited-after-propose no-op note has a scenario but no task instructing any body to detect or emit it
resolutions.action: Task 4.2 now requires the tail to COMPARE the frozen record against the change's current `.openspec.yaml` `architecture:` block and emit the one-line divergence note before acting (the frozen record still governs — the note keeps the no-op visible), plus a 6.2e harness case. The same read surfaced unrelated residue: task 4.2 still carried the pre-walk unconstrained `gh pr list --head <branch>` fallback that the external walk had already replaced with the four-axis query in the spec — corrected so task and requirement agree.

resolutions.title: Archive's AI-mediated consent preview is unmodified, so it under-describes the outward writes the tail now rides on
resolutions.action: Ratified option A. Added an EIGHTH delta block — MODIFIED `Consent prompt on AI-mediated archive entry` in `orbit-archive-modifications`, reproducing the baseline requirement and extending the preview: for a PR-ATTACHED change it additionally names the branch, the push to the resolved remote, and the READY flip (or the appended stage entry for a program PR). Justified at the point of the rule: the tail rides this same entry consent and fires no second prompt, so a preview enumerating only in-repo writes would obtain consent for a sync-and-move and then push to a remote and flip a PR public. Unattached changes keep the byte-identical pre-capability preview. Two new scenarios, task 4.5, fingerprint stamped (4/4 verified).
resolutions.resolution: A — add the eighth delta block so the consent preview names the outward writes

resolutions.title: Impact promises a CLAUDE.md D6 entry at archive; no task or at-archive note carries it
resolutions.action: Added at-archive note 5.9: add the D6 entry to root CLAUDE.md in the D1-D5 house style (what shipped, the cadence, the test count). Resolved toward the Impact bullet rather than against it — every prior stage carries such an entry, and it is what keeps CLAUDE.md accurate for the next cold start.

resolutions.title: "11 decisions" in proposal.md and design.md no longer matches explore.md's decision record
resolutions.action: Counted the record directly (12 Decisions bullets of which 2 are promotion-resolved; 6 post-promotion revisions; 5 rejections) and restated both summaries as '10 decisions + 2 promotion-resolved questions + 6 post-promotion revisions' (design.md also carries the 5 rejections), so the cadence's own revisions are visible from the summary docs rather than hidden behind a promotion-era number.

resolutions.title: At-archive notes are listed 5.5, 5.7, 5.8, 5.6 — the status-log entry reads as an afterthought
resolutions.action: Renumbered the at-archive notes monotonically in reading order: 5.5 stage-section retirement, 5.6 status-log entry, 5.7 single-session ruling, 5.8 subtraction exception, 5.9 CLAUDE.md entry. Ordering carries meaning here — the tail's program stage entry is specified to adapt the status-log entry written at the same archive, so the log note's position is the reader's cue about sequence.

final_assessment: 12 of 12 resolved; 0 unresolved markers in scope. Four decision-lane findings ratified in chat, all toward the structural rather than the cheaper option: skip-only HEAD verification, attachment authority over live config at the archive seam, a hoisted shared remote/default-branch resolution requirement consumed by both seams, and an eighth delta block extending the AI-mediated consent preview to name the tail's outward writes. Eight obvious-fix findings applied, two of which uncovered residue their finding did not name. Capabilities remain 7; delta blocks 8; tasks 26 to 29; fingerprints 4/4 verified; 1918 tests green.
